first_impression.reaction: My assistant flagged it, so I gave it the first screen. It's calm and doesn't oversell, which I liked. But it reads like a guide for any couple with a Filipino grandparent. Nothing on the first screen tells me this team has done a wedding for 300 guests with family flying in from three continents. I read on because the cultural detail is careful, not because it spoke to me.

journey.quote: Filipino wedding traditions are rarely written down in one place, and most families hold their own version.
journey.reaction: Good. It doesn't pretend there's one right way. That's the cultural awareness I want, without the stereotypes.

journey.section: Filipino wedding traditions at a glance
journey.quote: A Catholic family in Manila, a Protestant family in the Visayas and a Muslim family from the south may each describe a "traditional" Filipino wedding quite differently.
journey.reaction: This is the line that tells me they've thought about families like mine, where each side keeps different customs. I'd trust them with the elders more because of it.

journey.quote: For a destination wedding, a practical note: hold the pamamanhikan, or a version of it over dinner, before you lock the date.
journey.reaction: Sensible, and the kind of family protocol advice I'd actually pass on to my mother. But a dinner for two families is easy. With us it would be forty people over two cities. The guide never goes there.

journey.quote: Choosing secondary sponsors is a quiet way to honour siblings, cousins or close friends who are not in the bridal party.
journey.reaction: Useful, and tactful. In a family our size, deciding who gets a role is political, and this shows they understand that.

journey.quote: Some couples hold a basket or envelope nearby for guests who would rather not pin.
journey.reaction: Fine for most weddings. At ours, with VIP guests and cameras around, I'd want to know how they handle it discreetly, or whether we leave it out. The guide treats it as a guest-comfort question only.

journey.quote: Shortlist only places outside the higher-level areas, and recheck Smartraveller advice for the Philippines before you pay any deposits, since the page is updated regularly.
journey.reaction: Responsible. But if the advice is 'exercise a high degree of caution', my first question is security. Can the venue work with our own team, and who handles private transfers? There's nothing on that.

journey.section: Getting married in the Philippines as an Australian
journey.quote: One person works with you in your time zone, from first idea to the last dance.
journey.reaction: One person, for a wedding with 300 guests, our security and a family office? That makes the team sound small to me. And 'from first idea to the last dance' is a little too eager.

journey.quote: When you are ready to talk dates, families and paperwork, your Wedded Advisor is one conversation away.
journey.reaction: Polite enough, but it's the same door everyone walks through. I'd need a private channel or an introduction. And 'paperwork' is my assistant's job, not something I'd raise with a planner.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Wonderland delivered a Filipino or multicultural wedding at 200 to 400 guests?
Can they arrange exclusive use of a venue, in the Philippines or elsewhere, and close it to the public for several days?
How do they work with a private security team, and what do they do about guest phones, photography and press?
Who handles private transfers and VIP arrivals, given the Smartraveller caution level?
Is there a private or referral-only way to make first contact, or a senior person rather than one advisor?
Can they organise Filipino catering and family customs alongside guests travelling from Dubai, London and Sydney?

turn_offs_found.quote: One person works with you in your time zone, from first idea to the last dance.
turn_offs_found.why: Slightly eager phrasing, and 'one person' tells me the team isn't built for my scale.

would_share_with: My mother and aunts, for the sponsors and pamamanhikan sections

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk dates, families and paperwork, your Wedded Advisor is one conversation away.
cta_reaction.why: Nothing here shows they've handled my guest numbers, discretion or security, and I don't enquire through a general form. My assistant would note the name and wait for a referral.

top_3_changes: Add one understated line about large family weddings: guest numbers in the hundreds, families travelling from several countries, and sponsor and elder roles at that scale. Only if it can be backed up.
In the Smartraveller or destination section, mention exclusive use, working with private security and private transfers, so caution reads as a planning matter the team handles.
Rewrite 'One person works with you in your time zone, from first idea to the last dance' to sound less eager and less like a solo service, and offer a discreet or private way to make contact.

Is there any evidence of large-scale (200+ guest) or exclusive-use delivery that the post could refer to in an understated way?

assumptions: Layla has, or is marrying into, a family with Filipino heritage. The assistant shortlisted the post for that reason.
